titulo.alumno: I am looking for someone who knows

intro: Choose indicative or subjunctive in relative clauses according to whether the person or thing is identified.

palabras.consejo: In «busco un guía que sepa», the antecedent is «un guía». If it is not identified, subjunctive.
If the speaker has someone specific in mind, it is «identified»: indicative.
It is feminine: «la vacante». The v and b sound the same: ba-KAN-te.
It is masculine: «el requisito». You say «cumplir los requisitos».
The feminine is «candidata». The d is soft: kan-di-DA-to.
It has two meanings: «una plaza de trabajo» and «la plaza del pueblo». The z sounds «th».
It does not change in the feminine: «contrato temporal», «plaza temporal». The stress is at the end: tem-po-RAL.
«El guía» is a man; «la guía» is a woman or a book. It has an accent: GI-a.
It is written with «sc»: as-then-SOR. In America you also say «elevador».
It is masculine: «el informe». Do not mix it up with «informal» or «informar».
From «buscar», to look for. Stress on KA: bus-KA-mos.
Subjunctive of «conocer», to know. The c before o is k, and the z before a is th.
From «necesitar», to need. Stress on TA.
Subjunctive of «hablar», to speak. The h is silent: A-ble.
It means Arabic, both the language and the people. Stress on A.
Subjunctive of «cumplir», to fulfil. Stress on KUM.
Plural of «requisito», requirement. Stress on SI.
From «valorar», to value. The v sounds like b. Stress on RA.
Participle of «trabajar», to work. The j sounds like h. Stress on HA.
Future of «entrevistar», to interview. The v sounds like b. Stress on RE.
Subjunctive of «cumplir», plural. Stress on KUM: KUM-plan.
Plural of «condición», condition. The -ción ending takes the stress.
Future of «trabajar», to work. The j sounds like h. Stress on RA.
From «organizar», to organise. The z is th in Spain. Stress on NI.
Plural of «visita», visit. The v sounds like b. Stress on SI.
Plural of «escuela», school. The ue is a diphthong.
Subjunctive of «tener», to have. Stress on TEN: TEN-ga.
Subjunctive of «explicar», to explain. The x sounds ks.
Plural of «sala», a room or hall. Stress on SA.
Feminine plural of «pesado», heavy. Stress on SA.
From «amarillear», to turn yellow. The ll sound is y; the ea is two syllables.
Plural of «vitrina», display case. The v sounds like b. Stress on TRI.
From «guardar», to keep. The gu before a is gw: GWAR-dan.
Plural of «mapa», map. Stress on MA: MA-pas.
Plural of «reloj», clock. The j sounds like h. Stress on LO.
Future of «necesitar», to need. Stress on RA.
Feminine of «candidato». Stress on DA: kan-di-DA-ta.
Subjunctive of «subir», to go up. The b and v sound the same: SU-ba.
Masculine, «el origen». The g before e is h. Stress on RI.
Infinitive of «contener», to hold in. Stress on NER.
Masculine, «el aliento». The ie is a diphthong: a-LIEN-to.
Feminine of «identificado», identified. Stress on KA.
From «existir», to exist. The x sounds ks. Stress on IS.

texto:
A relative clause describes a person or thing. The choice of mood often depends on whether the speaker presents its antecedent as **identified and real**, or as **unknown, sought or nonexistent**.

- **Identified, presented as real: indicative.** Conozco a una periodista que **trabaja** en Quito. The speaker has a particular journalist in mind.
- **Unknown or sought: subjunctive.** Busco a una periodista que **trabaje** en Quito. The speaker has not identified that person.
- **No such person or thing exists: subjunctive.** No hay ningún informe que **explique** el resultado.
- **A real but not yet identified item can take the subjunctive.** Necesito un piso que **tenga** ascensor.

The subjunctive does not mean that the person or thing is unreal in the world; it marks how the speaker presents it in this sentence. Compare the context and meaning, not just the noun before **que**.

piezas.titulo: Indicative or subjunctive in the relative
texto:
- **Indicative**: the person or thing exists and is identified: conozco a una guía que habla árabe.
- **Subjunctive**: it is sought, wished for or nonexistent: busco una guía que hable árabe; no hay nadie que hable árabe.

**A trick**: ask yourself whether the speaker has someone specific in mind. If so, indicative; if not, subjunctive.

pregunta.texto: What is the guide like in «busco una guía que hable árabe»?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: someone not yet known is being sought.
Then you would say «conozco a una guía que habla árabe».
The subjunctive does not say that: it only marks that she is not identified.

pregunta.texto: You have not found him yet: choose the mood.

opciones.explicacion: Yes: something sought and unidentified takes the subjunctive.
It is indicative, for a guide you already know.
It is an infinitive. Here you need a conjugated verb.

frase.texto: No hay ningún informe que explique el resultado

piezas.traduccion: There is no report that explains the result

pregunta.texto: It is someone you already know: choose the mood.

frase.texto: Conozco a un guía que ____ árabe.

piezas.traduccion: Conozco a un guía que ____ árabe.

opciones.explicacion: Yes: an identified person takes the indicative.
It is subjunctive, for someone you do not know yet.
It is a past subjunctive and does not fit the present.

pregunta.texto: In «un equipo que organiza visitas», why the indicative?

opciones.explicacion: If it did not exist, it would take the subjunctive.

opciones.texto: porque el equipo existe y está identificado
opciones.explicacion: Well done: it is presented as a real, known group.
The sentence does not speak of the future, but of a real team.

pregunta.texto: Something nonexistent asks for the subjunctive.

frase.texto: No hay nadie que ____ la respuesta.

piezas.traduccion: No hay nadie que ____ la respuesta.

opciones.explicacion: Yes: what does not exist takes the subjunctive.
It is indicative; after «no hay nadie que» comes the subjunctive.
It is an infinitive. Here a conjugated verb goes.
